Good morning from DC. **Martin** here, making a claim to be the **Folarin
Balogun** of **Zeteo** FC - if only in that I'm American and British at the
same time, as I both wasn't born here and somehow doubt Donald Trump would
personally intervene to have me reprieved from a red card and freed to play
for the U.S. in a (rugby) World Cup.

Anyway. In today's **' First Draft,'** we take in a major development in
Michigan, where **Mallory McMorrow** dropped out of the Democratic U.S. Senate
primary on Sunday, leaving a straight fight between pro-Palestine progressive
**Abdul El-Sayed** and pro-Israel centrist **Haley Stevens**. All the issues
that have dominated recent House primaries won by left-wingers are present -
Medicare for All, corporate cash, AIPAC - and the polls look good for El-
Sayed. Elsewhere, Trump spent Sunday pretending he'd had a huge crowd for his
Saturday night 250th birthday speech, when he wasn't posting about his
repellent remodeling of DC, while talks to end his illegal Iran War remained
in limbo. There's all that and more to think about, so let's get started.

On Sunday, after state Senator Mallory McMorrow ended her campaign for the
Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate in Michigan, sources from either end of
the party considered the most telling part of her move: she chose not to
endorse.

Adam Green, co-founder of the [Progressive Change Campaign
Committee](https://www.boldprogressives.org/) (PCCC),
[said](https://x.com/BoldProgressive/status/2073861860059672651): **" Kudos to
Mallory McMorrow for not endorsing Haley Stevens."**

Though **" the DC establishment is sending a desperate signal to Michigan
voters that Haley Stevens is the status quo insider they want to rally
around,"** Green said, **" Abdul El-Sayed is the most important primary
candidate in America."**

Tellingly, Green found an echo from the heart of that establishment. Former
Obama strategist and White House adviser David Axelrod
[said](https://x.com/davidaxelrod/status/2073872262587973729?s=46): **"
Conventional thinking in DC has been that a Mallory McMorrow exit would help
Haley Stevens. But candidate quality matters, and Abdul El-Sayed is a strong
candidate. Stevens has big establishment support but he remains the
frontrunner."**

El-Sayed does enjoy [healthy polling
leads](https://fiftyplusone.news/polls/senate/democratic-primary/michigan).
The progressive choice opposed to Stevens, the party insider, like other left-
wingers who won recent primaries in [New York](https://zeteo.com/p/aipac-
loses-as-the-left-wins-big) and [Colorado](https://zeteo.com/p/aipac-defeated-
again-this-time-in), El-Sayed campaigns passionately for policies such as
Medicare for All, and passionately against influences such as AIPAC, the pro-
Israel lobby group that maintains a grip on much of Congress. Stevens, a
[former Obama adviser](https://stevens.house.gov/haleys-bio) in the House
since 2019, enjoys [massive AIPAC
support](https://forward.com/news/835898/aipac-michigan-senate-haley-stevens-
ice/).

After McMorrow announced her withdrawal [on social
media](https://www.instagram.com/p/Daa3x69kVgV/?hl=en), El-Sayed responded.
